cross_item_rule: Only one rule fired repeatedly, and it is an elimination rule, not a selection rule: in the notes items the options are held in ONE frame that varies a single value (a number, a label, or a 2x2 crossing of two labels), so every option satisfies the stem equally and only the withheld notes discriminate. That held on 1, 3, 5, 6, 18, 21 and partly 17 - about 7 of the 11 notes items - and it predicts I should be at chance there, which is what I expect. The two places it did NOT hold are where the options differ along an axis the stem does not control: item 10 (two of the four options assert the same late-increase shape, so neither can be the unique key) and items 13/19 (one variable is a real-world fact, not a note - clouding is a high-humidity defect, dung burns out and grog does not), which kills two options each. Item 14 is the same knowledge leak in weaker form. The 13 transition items gave me nothing at all; no shape, length, register or frame tell separated them, and I picked essentially at random.
shared_frames: Yes, three groupings. (1) The 2x2 label-crossing frame: 6, 13, 18, 19, 21 all cross two named entities against two attributes, so recognising the construction tells you the item is a pure notes-lookup and that two options are mirror-images - but solving one does not help another, since the pairings are independent. (2) The single-varying-number frame: 1, 3, 5 are identical in construction (fixed sentence, one figure swapped four ways); these are the cleanest items in the set. (3) The trend-shape frame: 10 and 17 both fix the endpoints and vary the shape of the path between them, and in both the near-duplicate-options test is the only available attack. The 13 transition items share a frame trivially (identical stem, four connectives) but carry no transferable information.
